analysis.title: "Investors See Ghosts Around Every Corner": Goldman Partner Says Don't Fight The Narrowness As Just 10 Stocks Drive 68% Of Q3 Earnings Growth
key_insights: Goldman's Mark Wilson says this week's news was fine (10Y auction, Samsung and TSMC records, French fiscal plans) but investors sold it anyway, which he attributes to fragile positioning and sentiment rather than fundamentals.
US fundamental long/short hedge fund net length is in the 1st percentile on a 1-year lookback. Global L/S net exposure was in the 5th percentile a week earlier, with US-only at 0%-2%.
Goldman's high-momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) fell from 848 on June 22 to 450 on Sept 3, a 47% peak-to-trough drop. After a bounce it is rolling over at 572, still about a third below its high.

Goldman's Shawn Tuteja says the prime book shows US L/S nets in the 2nd percentile on a five-year lookback. Net exposure to the Mag 7 is near 22% of total US exposure, the highest since the start of 2022. Global fundamental L/S funds ended June +17.4% and are now +12.5%.

Wilson attributes the bond selloff to a new regime: heavy AI-related private-sector financing (SpaceX, Broadcom, Oracle) now competes with sovereigns for funding. 98bps of the 108bps 10-year selloff is real rates, and the 30Y real yield is through 3% for the first time since 2010.

Rich Privorotsky says the crowding-out effect from private-sector AI debt issuance is potentially immense and may explain why real yields refuse to fall. Oracle's 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bps and Broadcom's at a record 136bps.

The 6-month correlation between the STOXX 600 and the 10Y bund yield is -0.7, the most negative outside 2022 since the late 1990s (Sharon Bell). Each 10bps rise in yields costs the STOXX 600 roughly 1-1.2%.

Wilson sees Europe as cheap: 22% EPS growth in 2H26 (15% ex-energy per Bell), 13x earnings, 5.5% FCF yield, steeply negative equity supply and near-average breadth. The top 10 stocks are about 17% of the STOXX 600 versus nearly 40% of the S&P.
French political risk limits the European case. The OAT-Bund spread reached 142bps, the widest since 2011. Bell estimates each 10bps of OAT and BTP spread widening takes 0.9% from Europe's PE.
Bottom-up consensus S&P 500 EPS growth for Q3 is 27%, the cycle high, with deceleration over the following three quarters (Ben Snider).

The top 10 contributors will make up 68% of SPX EPS growth in Q3, up from 48% last quarter and 54% estimated for Q4. Micron and Nvidia make up half of the 68%: Micron 19% of S&P earnings growth and Nvidia 15%.

Median S&P stock EPS growth is slowing from 14% to 9%, with margins slipping to 14.7% from 15.1%. Consensus growth falls to low single digits by Q2 2027, when the comparison includes about $150BN of mega-cap tech other income from marked-up equity stakes.
Breadth is poor. Nomura's McElligott says 85% of S&P names are more than 10% below their highs and 59% are more than 20% below. Since Aug 27 the S&P is +1.3% while the S&P ex-AI is -5.2% (Tuteja).

Wilson's conclusion is to not fight narrowness. He expects hyperscaler capex growth to peak this quarter well above 100% (consensus 116%) and leadership to rotate from AI suppliers to the biggest AI spenders. A year-end rally requires stability in energy prices.

Dissenting views: Tuteja says the Tech/AI asymmetry has shifted and all sectors have near-term downside if CPI prints high. Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson says poor breadth must be resolved and hinges on bond vol. BofA's Hartnett reports $166.4BN into money market funds in the week to Oct 7, the most since April 2020.
McElligott sees S&P call skew in the 99.6th percentile, so the vol market is pricing fear of a right-tail rally. He warns higher rates and energy could 'Break Something' and trigger a growth scare.

Market backdrop cited by the author: the 30Y auction priced at 5.618%, the highest yield since August 2000. The 10Y auction stopped through by 1.7bps. Brent is at $103, a hurricane shut in 63% of Gulf of Mexico output, and Iran is hitting tankers outside Hormuz.

market_movers.rationale: Micron is expected to contribute 19% of S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth, more than Meta, Alphabet and Amazon combined (Goldman's Snider).
Nvidia is expected to contribute 15% of S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth. Wilson expects underinvested hedge funds to be pulled into Micron and Nvidia by December.
Oracle's 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bps as it joins the AI chip-debt financing wave.
Broadcom's 5Y CDS closed at a record 136bps, with $50BN-plus of financing chatter.

sector_views.rationale: Wilson expects equities to rally into year-end if capex continues and energy stabilizes, with leadership rotating from AI suppliers to the biggest AI spenders. Tuteja is more cautious on the Tech/AI asymmetry.
Wilson cites 22% 2H26 EPS growth (15% ex-energy), 13x earnings, 5.5% FCF yield, negative equity supply and M&A at pre-GFC highs. Offsetting risk is French spread widening.
French banks fell 4% on Wednesday as the OAT-Bund spread reached 142bps, the widest since 2011.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth: bottom-up consensus estimate of 27% (Goldman's Snider), the cycle high, with deceleration over the next three quarters. This is an estimate, not a reported figure.
Top 10 contributors are estimated at 68% of Q3 S&P EPS growth, versus 48% in Q2 and an estimated 54% in Q4. Micron and Nvidia together are estimated at half of the 68%.
Median S&P stock EPS growth is estimated to slow from 14% to 9%, with margins at 14.7% versus 15.1% (consensus estimates).
Samsung reported a fourth straight record quarter and the stock slipped 1%. TSMC reported Q3 revenue of NT$1.49 trillion, above the top end of guidance.
Europe 2H26 EPS growth consensus is 22%, or 15% ex-energy (Bell).
Hyperscaler capex growth is expected to peak this quarter 'well north of 100%' (Wilson) versus consensus of 116%. Bank earnings begin with JPMorgan on Tuesday.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest auction yield since August 2000, showing weak demand for long-duration sovereign paper amid heavy private-sector AI debt supply.
A strong auction by the numbers, yet the market still sold off.
The rise is driven by real yields rather than inflation expectations.
First time through 3% since the series began in 2010.
Widest since the 2011 euro crisis, driven by French fiscal and political concerns.
Lowest in about a decade, supporting Wilson's view that private balance sheets are healthy.
Largest weekly inflow since April 2020, indicating heavy cash hoarding.
Seen as the next potential circuit breaker for the bond selloff. Tuteja warns a high print that forces the Fed to act would hurt all sectors.

trade_ideas.description: Wilson's stance: do not fight market narrowness. Expect equities to rally into year-end if investment activity continues and energy prices stabilize, with leadership rotating from AI suppliers to the biggest AI spenders.
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning is washed out at the 1st percentile and AI capex demand remains strong.
trade_ideas.risk: Yields stay high, energy prices spike, or CPI prints high and forces a Fed response.

risk_factors: A high CPI print next week could force Fed tightening and cause downside across all sectors (Tuteja).
Continued heavy AI-related private debt issuance may keep real yields elevated and crowd out sovereign debt.
Energy price instability (Brent at $103, Gulf hurricane, Iran tanker attacks) could undermine the year-end rally scenario.
French fiscal and political risk could further widen OAT and BTP spreads, taking about 0.9% from European PE per 10bps.
Extreme market narrowness, with two stocks contributing about a third of S&P EPS growth, leaves index earnings exposed to a miss at Micron or Nvidia.
Higher rates and energy could 'Break Something' and trigger a growth scare (McElligott).
Median S&P stock margins are slipping, and EPS growth faces a tough comparison in Q2 2027 against about $150BN of other income from marked-up equity stakes.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson says not to fight narrowness. Funds are at 1st percentile positioning, AI capex demand is insatiable, and hyperscaler capex peaks well above 100%, so equities can rally to year-end as leadership rotates to AI spenders.
tension_points.bear_case: Two stocks deliver about a third of S&P EPS growth, growth peaks this quarter, median EPS growth slows to 9%, AI debt issuance crowds out sovereigns, and Tuteja says the Tech/AI asymmetry has shifted.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A high CPI print next week forcing the Fed to act, or energy prices failing to stabilize (Brent at $103), would undermine the year-end rally.

tension_points.theme: European equity valuation vs French risk
tension_points.bull_case: Europe is on 13x earnings with 5.5% FCF yield, 22% 2H26 EPS growth, negative equity supply, healthy breadth and M&A at pre-GFC levels.
tension_points.bear_case: EU decision-making is more complex, so Europe is more vulnerable to market forces. French spreads have limited scope to retrace, and each 10bps of OAT and BTP widening takes 0.9% from European PE.

theme_stances.key_argument: Don't fight market narrowness, which may get even more extreme, as long as investment activity continues and energy prices stabilize.
theme_stances.evidence: don't fight market narrowness; it may well get even more extreme

theme_stances.key_argument: It is undoubtedly tougher for equities to make meaningful progress in the face of higher rates in a new regime.
theme_stances.evidence: this is a new regime investors haven't dealt with for decades

theme_stances.key_argument: Positioning this washed out tends to force funds back into Micron and Nvidia by December.
